findings.title: Same-timestamp staking injects post-snapshot voting power
findings.root_cause: propose() snapshots totalVotingPower at block.timestamp, but votingPowerAt() accepts checkpoints with timestamp <= the snapshot, so power staked later in the same transaction counts for the attacker's vote while being absent from the quorum denominator.

findings.title: Mutable quorum retroactively changes completed proposal outcomes
findings.root_cause: The Governor snapshots total voting power but evaluates every proposal against the current global quorumBps, so changing quorum revives defeated proposals (which never expire) or defeats already-queued ones.

findings.title: Automatic fee sales can under-mint liquidity additions
findings.root_cause: Every transfer to the pair is treated as a sale, so the router's addLiquidityETH transfer triggers an automatic fee swap after the router has priced the contribution, leaving the LP with stale ratios and fewer LP tokens.

findings.title: Uncaught automation failures can block sells and liquidity bootstrap
findings.root_cause: Fee sales, buybacks and payouts run synchronously inside _transfer before the user's transfer with no failure isolation, so any revert in the automation reverts sells and liquidity adds.

findings.title: Dust transfers bypass aggregate automation pacing
findings.root_cause: Per-call limits are the only constraint on automated fee sales and buybacks; there is no per-block or per-epoch cap, so repeated dust transfers to the pair trigger the automation as often as an attacker likes.

findings.title: Reflections accrued by the AMM pair can be permissionlessly skimmed
findings.root_cause: Only deadAddress is excluded from reflections, so the PancakeSwap pair's balance grows with reflection fees above its reserves and anyone can skim() the excess.

findings.title: Reflection accrued by Staking is unrecoverable through current interfaces
findings.root_cause: The Staking contract is fee-excluded but still reflection-included, so its token balance grows passively beyond tracked principal and no function can distribute or recover that surplus.

findings.title: A minimal first stake can atomically capture the zero-staker reward backlog
findings.root_cause: Rewards arriving while totalVotingPower is zero accumulate in undistributedRewards and the next notification distributes the whole backlog to current stakers, so a 1-wei first stake captures it all.

findings.title: Guardian can indefinitely censor governance and preserve a global pause
findings.root_cause: guardianExpiry only stops a new pause from being set; a pause set before expiry persists, and the same guardian's Governor cancel and Timelock CANCELLER_ROLE powers never expire, so the guardian can block governance from lifting it.
